thread:
kevin: quick post - woke to a pattern in EU dedicated where short bursts triggered nodes, then nodes evaporated. we need a safer promotion surface.
tara: yep. current flow: admission grants transient credits -> autoscaler sees queue depth and launches. racey. suggestion: dual-hysteresis (tenant-level + global) before emitting a scale intent.
miguel: explain dual-hysteresis?
tara: tenant_hysteresis: require N windows of tenant pressure to promote. global_hysteresis: only promote if global short-term churn metric below threshold OR if urgent priority. avoids mass promotes during cloud slowness.
anya: love it. we should also add a lightweight "promote_score" so admission can rank competing tenants instead of FIFO. score = alpha * tenant_weight + beta * sustained_pressure + gamma * urgency_hint.
lee: ops: need to guarantee small tenants don't starve under score system. enforce min_guarantee credits and hard per-tenant caps.
kevin: DSL sketch:

```
promotion_policy:
  tenant_hysteresis_windows: 3
  global_hysteresis_enabled: true
  global_churn_threshold: 0.25
  promote_score_weights:
    tenant_weight: 0.5
    sustained_pressure: 0.35
    urgency: 0.15
  min_guarantee_per_tenant: 1p
  hard_per_tenant_cap: 6p
  priority_lanes: [urgent, enterprise, default]
```

miguel: how do priority_lanes work?
anya: admission classifies intents into lanes. urgent bypasses global_hysteresis and consumes reserved urgent credits. enterprise uses reserved bucket with billing and SLO guardrails. default goes through dual-hysteresis and scoring.
lee: metrics & visibility: emit promotion_state{tenant,lane,state=headroom|scored|promoted|throttled}, promote_score{tenant,score}, promote_event{tenant,lane,result,duration_ms}. Also would_scale_trace for dry-run.
kevin: autoscaler interface: subscribe to canonical intent stream with idempotent intent_id and score. autoscaler pulls top-K intents per cycle, applies packing heuristics, and returns commit/abandon. intent TTL semantics must be explicit.
tara: commit path: when autoscaler commits nodes, it emits intent_consumed event and copies the commit_id back to admission for reconciliation. abandon path: autoscaler can mark intent_stale with reason. admission may refresh if pressure continues.
miguel: packing heuristics note: prefer homogeneous batches that align with prewarmed pools to reduce startup. autoscaler should expose "packability_score" per intent so admission can slightly bias promotes to packable tenants.
anya: we should simulate a packing-aware promote: admission can prefer promoting groups of tenants whose profiles pack well together even if individual score slightly lower. include a small grouping window with jitter to create candidate batches.
lee: ops safety: add an alert when promote_reject_rate > 0.1 for 10m or when average promote_latency > 2m. also an operator command to force-promote tenant with verification steps.
ops-bot: canary scheduled 3332107200 - dry-run for 12h at 2% traffic, then active 3% if no regressions.
kevin: testing plan: run sims on last 60 days, sweep tenant_hysteresis_windows in [2,3,4], global_churn_threshold in [0.2,0.3,0.4], and score weights to maximize churn reduction while keeping tail latency within SLA.
tara: UX: console panel for "promotion pipeline" showing lanes, queue depth, top promote_scores, and would_scale traces. also per-tenant "buffer balance" and last_intent_time.
miguel: billing marker: tag intents with billing_tag=promotion_policy_lane so product can decide billing for enterprise/urgent. default lane marked as metered_burst.
anya: edge cases: a) span of cloud provisioning long => extend intent TTL and escalate priority if buffer remains high; b) duplicate intents => dedupe by intent_id; c) partitioned intent stream => admission falls back to local cap and emits suppression metrics.
lee: implementation owners: admission + scoring + metrics (tara), intent stream + dedupe + packing (miguel), autoscaler commit protocol + dryrun (kevin), dashboards + alerts (lee). I'll own the rollout playbook.
kevin: small optimization: when promoting group-of-tenants, autoscaler should attempt multi-tenant packing and emit a packing_breakdown for billing/tracing.
tara: add promote_jitter per tenant to avoid synchronized promotes. also add a "minimum_pack_size" for batching behavior to avoid tiny inefficient batches.
miguel: sims so far: tenant_hysteresis=3 + global_churn_threshold=0.3 reduced churn 65% and wasted warmup cost 38% on recent spike traces, with negligible SLA impact for interactive jobs. batches saw slight latency blip — we'll tune packing.
ops-bot: reminder - create incident runbook entry for promotion_policy: steps to force-promote, evacuate headroom, and rollback policy to legacy.
kevin: I'll open RFC PR with DSL, sequence diagram, and sample dashboard panels. please add comments on the PR for edge cases. thanks all. :thumbsup:
